Classic Green Bean Casserole

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 6-8Prep 10 minCook 35-40 min

Green Bean Casserole is a quintessential side dish that graces nearly every Thanksgiving table across the United States. This creamy, savory bake, topped with crispy fried onions, offers a comforting contrast to the richer flavors of the holiday feast, making it a beloved and eagerly anticipated part of the annual celebration.

Ingredients

  • 2 (14.5 ounce / 411 g) cans cut green beans, drained
  • 1 (10.5 ounce / 298 g) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
  • 1/2 cup (120 mL) milk
  • 1 teaspoon (5 mL) soy sauce
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 mL) black pepper
  • 1 (6 ounce / 170 g) can French fried onions

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the condensed cream of mushroom soup, milk, soy sauce, and black pepper. Stir until the mixture is smooth and well blended.
  3. Add the drained green beans and 1/2 of the French fried onions to the soup mixture. Stir gently to ensure the beans are evenly coated.
  4. Pour the entire mixture into a 1.5-quart (1.4 L) casserole dish.
  5. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the casserole is hot and bubbly.
  6. Remove the casserole from the oven and sprinkle the remaining French fried onions evenly over the top.
  7. Return the casserole to the oven and bake for an additional 5-10 minutes, or until the onions are golden brown and crispy.
  8. Serve hot and enjoy this classic holiday side dish.

Tips

  • For a fresher take, substitute canned green beans with 1.5 pounds (680 g) fresh green beans, trimmed and blanched, or 2 (10 ounce / 283 g) packages frozen green beans, thawed.
  • Add 1/2 cup (50 g) shredded sharp cheddar cheese or a sprinkle of crumbled cooked bacon to the mixture before baking for an extra layer of flavor.
  • Ensure your French fried onions are fresh; stale onions won't achieve the desired crispiness.
